questions.stem: Which gases are the main causes of acid rain?

options.text: Hydrogen and helium
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
Carbon monoxide and methane
Oxygen and nitrogen

questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) dissolve in rainwater to form sulfuric acid and nitric acid respectively, creating acid rain.

questions.stem: How does sulfur dioxide form sulfuric acid in the atmosphere?

options.text: It dissolves in rainwater and reacts with oxygen and water to form sulfuric acid
It reacts with nitrogen to form an acid
It condenses directly into an acid
It reacts with carbon dioxide to form an acid

questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rainwater and reacts with oxygen and water in the atmosphere to form sulfuric acid (H2SO4), which falls as acid rain.

questions.stem: What effect does acid rain have on limestone buildings and statues?

options.text: It changes their colour to green
It makes them stronger
It corrodes and dissolves them because the acid reacts with calcium carbonate
It has no effect on buildings

questions.explanation: Acid rain reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone and marble, dissolving and corroding buildings, statues, and monuments over time. The reaction produces a soluble salt, water, and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: How does acid rain affect lakes and rivers?

options.text: It makes the water more alkaline
It increases the number of fish
It lowers the pH, making the water acidic, which can kill fish and other aquatic organisms
It makes the water evaporate faster

questions.explanation: Acid rain lowers the pH of lakes and rivers. Many aquatic organisms cannot survive in acidic conditions, and acid rain can also release toxic metal ions from soil into the water.

questions.stem: What effect does acid rain have on trees and vegetation?

options.text: It damages leaves, leaches minerals from soil, and can kill trees
It has no effect on plant life
It helps them grow faster
It only affects plants in deserts

questions.explanation: Acid rain damages leaves directly, leaches essential minerals from the soil that trees need to grow, and releases toxic aluminium ions that damage root systems, weakening and potentially killing trees.

questions.stem: How can the amount of sulfur dioxide released from power stations be reduced?

options.text: By adding more sulfur to the fuel
By burning more coal
By building taller chimneys
By using flue gas desulfurisation to remove SO2 from waste gases before they leave the chimney

questions.explanation: Flue gas desulfurisation removes sulfur dioxide from waste gases by reacting it with calcium oxide or calcium carbonate. This prevents the SO2 from entering the atmosphere and causing acid rain.

questions.stem: Why can acid rain fall far from the source of the pollution that causes it?

options.text: Because acid rain only forms in tropical countries
Because acid rain is attracted to clean air
Because acid rain travels through underground rivers
Because the pollutant gases can be carried long distances by prevailing winds before dissolving in rain

questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides can be carried hundreds or even thousands of kilometres by prevailing winds before they dissolve in rainwater and fall as acid rain, often in a different country from where the pollution originated.
